accepted_edits.reason: these edits answer the review's own findings, each recorded with --acted

findings.reason: a worker dispatched to this section is given two incompatible acceptance tests and will read one of them wrong, so the per-node hold it exists to add either is not built or reports falsely.
findings.text: §6 requires a section's node to be held while its sibling node stays ready, but the roadmap's ready_sections is built as a list of section ids (`item["section"] for item in row["section_readiness`) and carries no node, so the same section cannot be absent from ready_sections in one bullet and queueable by a second node in the next

findings.reason: a node can pass every named test while neither clause is implemented, which is exactly the D50 "attempt in flight" refusal the section exists to remove.
findings.text: §9's deliverable states that a coordinator resume with advice supersedes an automatic repair round that has not started its worker, and that every resume prints a transition row, but the done-when tests only the advice hold, the two released holders, and the resume-mark case; never the supersede and never the transition row

findings.reason: a worker can deliver a flag fix, pass the one control, and be closed on a verdict that proves neither of the other two behaviours.
findings.text: §15 combines three separately failable outcomes — flag spelling, followup author/date defaults, and resolving a committed plan in a sprint append — under one verdict, and its single negative control (archived: true) exercises only the first, though the section was split from §14 precisely to stop outcomes that succeed or fail independently sharing a node

findings.reason: the clause is the remedy for that observed defect and nothing in the node's gate would fail if it were omitted.
findings.text: §7's Why cites "the promoted §2 row also recorded no plan slug" and the deliverable requires every promoted row to carry its plan slug, but none of the four done-when cases reads a promoted row's plan slug

response_events.note: §6's ready-set case is per node: a section whose only node has a promoted run is absent, one with a second unqueued node stays listed
§9's done-when adds the coordinator-advice supersede and the transition row on every resume
§15 now has one test and one base-revision negative control per case; the three stay one section as one op surface, each separately verdicted
§7's done-when reads the plan slug on the ledger row a promotion writes for an implementation run

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited commit 1e9c272ea7 and tests/test_the_reflex_resumes_an_unpromoted_run.py both resolve at the reviewed base; the cited plans a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline, the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once, a-landing-never-waits-on-a-shared-index and work-flows-to-the-lane all exist under docs/plans/, and the refusal text "leaves the worker to infer intent" resolves to reckon/crew/node.py:1424.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §9's deliverable carries two clauses its done-when never exercises, and §7's promoted-row-plan-slug clause is likewise untested.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each gated section writes its log to the section's evidence fragment, and no section names a temporary or session-scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name or ticket number is carried into a named symbol in any in-scope unit; defect ids (D28, D98…) appear only as prose citations holding the plan's own evidence.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6's two done-when bullets cannot both hold under the roadmap's section-granular ready set, so the per-node hold it specifies has no readable endpoint for a split section.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §15 carries three independently failable deliverables (flag coercion, followup defaults, sprint append) under one verdict, with a negative control covering only the first.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the only declared wire is plan-after to work-flows-to-the-lane, and the sections declare themselves mutually independent; no depends-on is claimed that a section's content contradicts.
